D241.call_notes:
Rep: Good afternoon, Teodoro, and thank you for making time again. I understand Annelise has joined us this time.
Teodoro Jessamy (Office Manager): Yes, thank you. Annelise, this is the gentleman who walked me through the demo last week.
Annelise Galbraith (VP Finance): Good afternoon. I have read the proposal in full. I will be candid, I am not here to ask about the platform. The demo was clear, and the figures were in line with what we had pencilled in.
Rep: Then may I ask what you would like to cover?
Annelise Galbraith (VP Finance): Our position, mainly. The board met on Tuesday and, as of the new fiscal quarter, all discretionary projects across the network are paused. Not cancelled, paused. Capital and operating both.
Teodoro Jessamy (Office Manager): And, to be fair, Gwendolyn, who was sponsoring this on the leadership side, has accepted a post at another district. So I am, I suppose, a project without a patron at the moment.
Rep: I am sorry to hear that. Is there a date by which the pause is reviewed?
Annelise Galbraith (VP Finance): The language was 'until the spring', which, as you will appreciate, is not a date. We have five states of staff on three different payroll arrangements, and none of it is going to change before then.
Teodoro Jessamy (Office Manager): We are not speaking to anyone else, for what it is worth. I want to be clear on that. Nobody else has been shortlisted. We simply cannot proceed.
Rep: Understood. Would it be appropriate if I checked in after the new year?
Annelise Galbraith (VP Finance): I would rather you did than did not. Perhaps early March. By then we shall know who is sitting in Gwendolyn's chair, and what the budget looks like.
Teodoro Jessamy (Office Manager): Yes. March. I shall make a note.

D242.call_notes:
Rep: Thaddeus, great to see you again, and Kofi, welcome, I'm glad you could join.
Thaddeus Quillfeather (Chief People Officer): Thanks, thanks. So, Kofi, you missed the first bit, but honestly the thing that stuck with me was how fast the demo came together. We talked on, what, Monday? And by Thursday there you were, showing us the real thing with our actual shift patterns in it. I didn't have time to forget why I'd called.
Kofi Valdivia (CFO): I've got questions, I'll warn you. Mostly about what happens in month two when everything's live and something breaks.
Rep: Fair. Ask away.
Kofi Valdivia (CFO): Who do I call? A person, or a ticket queue?
Thaddeus Quillfeather (Chief People Officer): Oh, that was the other thing, Kofi, I emailed their support with a silly question last week, just testing really, and I had an answer in about twenty minutes. A real answer. Not 'we have received your request'.
Kofi Valdivia (CFO): Okay. And the rollout, is it six weeks or is it a year?
Rep: Six weeks for your size, and we've put the dates in the plan I sent.
Kofi Valdivia (CFO): Fine. I've got what I need. Thaddeus, I'm good if you're good.
Thaddeus Quillfeather (Chief People Officer): I'm good. I'm really good, actually. I was dreading this, and now I'm sort of looking forward to it.
D242.closing_email:
Subject: Elmcroft Fabrication, moving ahead

Hi,

Just a quick note to say we're going with Lanternmere HR. Kofi and I talked it through after the call and we're both comfortable.

Honestly, what tipped it for me was how quickly you got us a demo and that it actually covered our shift setup, plus the fact that support wrote back in minutes when I tested them. Kofi liked the six-week rollout plan, and he does not like much.

Can you send the paperwork over? Once it's signed I'll get our payroll lead looped in so we can start on the data cleanup.

Thanks for making this easy.

Thaddeus

D243.call_notes:
Rep: Jules, Amara, thanks for jumping on. I know you're both busy.
Jules Yarrow (COO): Let's be quick, then. We've gone through the demo, Amara's seen the recording. I'll say it straight: we like it, but it doesn't fit.
Rep: Fit in what sense?
Jules Yarrow (COO): Money. You came in at about nineteen thousand a year for our 148 people. Call it a hundred and thirty, a hundred and thirty-five a head per year. Tallyhold is quoting us just under twelve thousand all in. That's a seven thousand dollar gap, every year, in a business where margins on a good month are thin.
Amara Lindgren (Operations Director): And hospitality payroll swings. Seasonal bumps, tips, people on and off. We can't carry a fixed cost that's heavier than we need.
Rep: Is there any room if we looked at the module mix?
Jules Yarrow (COO): Maybe, but I doubt it gets close to twelve.
Amara Lindgren (Operations Director): There's one other thing, and it's small. We hire constantly, and Tallyhold has an applicant tracking piece built in. You don't. I'd have lived without it, honestly, we're using spreadsheets now anyway.
Jules Yarrow (COO): Right, that's a nice-to-have. The number is the number.
Rep: I understand. I'll send you a trimmed quote today in case it changes the picture.
Jules Yarrow (COO): Send it. But don't hold your breath. We're probably signing with them by Friday.
Amara Lindgren (Operations Director): Thanks for being straightforward with us throughout.

D244.call_notes:
Rep: Nadia, Amara, thanks for making the time. Where would you like to start?
Nadia Ashgrove (VP of People): Let me give you the update, because it affects everything. Amara, jump in if I get any of this wrong.
Amara Abernethy (CFO): Go ahead.
Nadia Ashgrove (VP of People): When we spoke in September, the plan was a go-live on January 1, with open enrolment running through November. As of last Thursday that is off. The board approved a hiring and systems freeze through at least the end of Q2. That covers 107 employees across four states and three separate payroll runs, none of which will change.
Amara Abernethy (CFO): To be precise, it's the FY27 operating plan. We were projecting a 6 percent revenue shortfall in the second half, and the trustees decided to hold all new commitments until the enrolment numbers for spring are known. Last year we came in at 412 students under target, and nobody wants a repeat.
Nadia Ashgrove (VP of People): So I want to be clear, because I know how this sounds. Your demo answered the questions on my list, 11 of 12. The implementation timeline was sound. I would have recommended this.
Amara Abernethy (CFO): The quote was fine too. I have no complaint about the number.
Nadia Ashgrove (VP of People): We have not spoken to another vendor. We have not even opened the Tallyhold email that came in. The whole thing is parked.
Rep: Would it make sense for me to pencil in a conversation for late spring?
Amara Abernethy (CFO): I'd say after the April board meeting. April 22, I believe.
Nadia Ashgrove (VP of People): And Sandra, our chair, has also been talking about a leadership review, so the priorities may shift again. I'll let you know where things land. Honestly, I'd rather still be doing this with you than starting over.
Rep: Understood. I'll reach out the week after April 22.
Nadia Ashgrove (VP of People): Perfect.

D245.call_notes:
Rep: Oriel, Nadia, good to have you both. I think we've got forty minutes?
Oriel Cadogan (Operations Manager): Let's use them. I'll cut to it. The demo was fine. The payroll side looks solid. My problem is vacation.
Rep: Time-off accrual?
Oriel Cadogan (Operations Manager): Yes. We've got two offices, one in Ohio and one in Illinois, and the policies are different. In Ohio it's front-loaded, everyone gets their eighty hours on January first. In Illinois it's accrual per pay period, and it has a carryover cap, plus the payout rules when someone leaves. Your system wants one policy per company.
Nadia Yarrow (CFO): One policy template per company, right. That's what your person said on the demo.
Rep: Right, what we can do is create two groups and set the accrual by hand for each.
Oriel Cadogan (Operations Manager): By hand. Every pay period. For one hundred ninety-three people. No. That's a spreadsheet with a login.
Nadia Yarrow (CFO): And it's a liability line on my balance sheet. If somebody's accrual is wrong, I'm the one who finds out at audit.
Oriel Cadogan (Operations Manager): Tallyhold handles it by location. It was in their demo, I watched it work. Price was not the issue. You were within a few hundred dollars of each other.
Rep: Is there any chance a workaround, or something on our roadmap, would change that?
Oriel Cadogan (Operations Manager): If it were live, maybe. Roadmap, no. We need to switch by March.
Nadia Yarrow (CFO): Sorry. It's a good product otherwise.
D245.closing_email:
Subject: Re: next steps

Hi,

Thanks for the time over the last few weeks. We've decided to go with Tallyhold. The deciding factor was being able to set vacation accrual rules separately for our Ohio and Illinois offices, which we couldn't do with Lanternmere today.

We appreciated the straight answers. If that changes down the road, I'll let you know.

Oriel

D246.call_notes:
Rep: Soren, Annelise, thank you both for joining. I wanted to follow up on the proposal.
Soren Brannigan (Operations Manager): Yes. Thank you for your patience, and thanks again for the demo earlier in the week. It was very well organised.
Annelise Fonseca (CFO): I appreciate you taking the time as well.
Soren Brannigan (Operations Manager): I wanted to let you know personally, rather than by email. We have decided to go in a different direction.
Rep: I see. Thank you for telling me directly. Is there anything we could have done differently, or anything you would be willing to share?
Soren Brannigan (Operations Manager): I would not say so, no. Everyone on your team was lovely to deal with. We have simply made a change, and I wanted to be courteous about it.
Annelise Fonseca (CFO): It has been a pleasure, truly. We are grateful for the effort that went into this.
Rep: That is kind. If you ever want to revisit, our door is open.
Soren Brannigan (Operations Manager): We will keep that in mind. Please pass on our thanks to the colleague who ran the demo.
Annelise Fonseca (CFO): Yes, please do. And best of luck to you all.
Rep: And to you both. Take care.
Soren Brannigan (Operations Manager): Thank you. Goodbye for now.

D247.call_notes:
Rep: Annelise, Linnea, thanks for hopping on again.
Annelise Fairweather (HR Generalist): Sure. Sorry, I'm on my third coffee and it's not even ten. Linnea, you can take the lead, I'll fill in the gaps.
Linnea Fonseca (HR Director): Okay. So, the honest answer is we're not moving forward, and I'd rather tell you why than make something up.
Rep: I'd appreciate that.
Linnea Fonseca (HR Director): Approvals. We have purchase requests, pay changes, new-hire offers. Each one goes through three, sometimes four people, and which four depends on the department and the dollar amount. Annelise has this flowchart that looks like a subway map.
Annelise Fairweather (HR Generalist): It's awful. But it's ours. And in the demo you showed us one approver, or two in a row. I asked about conditional routing and it was, uh, 'we'd have to look into that'.
Linnea Fonseca (HR Director): Right. We can't rebuild the whole thing around a tool. Not at this point, and not with 166 people.
Rep: And the alternative you're moving toward?
Linnea Fonseca (HR Director): Tallyhold, probably. Our broker's been pushing it for a while, and I trust her, she handles the renewals every year so she knows our mess. But that's not why. If your workflows had done the thing we need, I'd have had that conversation with her.
Annelise Fairweather (HR Generalist): Pricing was fine, by the way. Nobody's complaining about that.
Rep: Thanks for the candour, it helps.
Linnea Fonseca (HR Director): I'm sorry it's not better news. You were all good about it.

D248.call_notes:
Rep: Kwame, Fenella, thanks for squeezing this in.
Kwame Ivarsson (HR Generalist): Oh, no problem. So, I should say upfront, I'm not sure how this is going to go, because honestly, I'm not sure either. I mean, I know what I want, but, well, Fenella, why don't you say it?
Fenella Okonkwo (Finance Director): It's simple enough. We've put the whole systems project on hold. Our CEO is out on leave from the first of the month, and the interim has said no new vendors until she's back. That's, what, ten weeks at least. Probably more.
Kwame Ivarsson (HR Generalist): And I was her champion, sort of. The CEO's. She was the one who said 'fix payroll, it's embarrassing.' So now that she's gone, nobody else is pushing, and I'm not going to push on my own. I'd be, like, the guy pushing a boulder.
Rep: That makes sense. Has anything changed on our side that matters?
Kwame Ivarsson (HR Generalist): No, no. The demo was good. Wasn't it good, Fenella?
Fenella Okonkwo (Finance Director): It was fine. And I'll say, the number was on the high side for us, we'd have had to stretch a bit. But that's not the thing. The thing is nobody's allowed to sign anything.
Kwame Ivarsson (HR Generalist): We haven't talked to anyone else, just so you know. We're still stuck with what we've got. Spreadsheets and prayer.
Rep: Mind if I check in around the new year?
Kwame Ivarsson (HR Generalist): Please. Honestly, please do. Maybe by then I'll have a boss again.
D248.closing_email:
Subject: Pausing for now

Hi,

Just writing to confirm what we discussed. Our CEO is on leave and the interim has frozen new vendor decisions until she's back, so we're pausing the payroll project. We haven't picked anybody else.

Please do check in early in the new year. I'd like to pick this up again once things settle.

Thanks for your patience,
Kwame

D249.call_notes:
Rep: Bram, Ravi, thanks for making time. I want to make sure I understand where you landed after the second demo.
Bram Eastwood (Operations Manager): Sure. I'll go through the scoring sheet, because Ravi and I did one. Payroll, twenty-two out of twenty-five. Benefits administration, twenty-one. Onboarding, twenty-four. Then the recruiting category, and that's where it fell apart. Four.
Rep: Applicant tracking.
Bram Eastwood (Operations Manager): Yes. We hired forty-one people last year, 135 headcount, so that's thirty percent turnover in a software shop. We're running candidates through a separate tool at about eleven hundred a month, and half of the point of this project was to fold that in. Your platform doesn't have it. Your rep said it was on a roadmap, but no date.
Ravi Nakamura (Finance Director): And I was fine with the cost of the platform itself. I'll note that. The numbers worked if we could cancel the other subscription. If we can't, the total is higher than what we pay today.
Bram Eastwood (Operations Manager): On a separate note, and I don't want you to take this as the reason, the mobile app drove my team a bit nuts. Twice during the trial it logged three people out in the middle of submitting time off. They had to re-enter everything, one guy gave up. It's a small thing, I'll admit.
Rep: Noted, and I'll pass that along.
Bram Eastwood (Operations Manager): Fine. But the recruiting piece is it. We're going with a suite that has it built in.
Ravi Nakamura (Finance Director): Appreciate the candour from your side too.

D250.call_notes:
Rep: Signe, Bram, thanks for picking up. I know it's been a while.
Signe Galbraith (Chief People Officer): It has. Let's just say that out loud. Fourteen days. We first spoke on the, what, the second? And the demo was the sixteenth. In my world, two weeks is an eternity.
Rep: I'm sorry about the wait. Our calendar was tight.
Signe Galbraith (Chief People Officer): I know, I know. I'm not blaming anybody. But I had a window. My CEO said, find something by month end or we do nothing this year. I had energy on the second. By the sixteenth I was running around fixing a benefits mix-up and, honestly, he'd lost interest. I'd lost some too.
Bram Dunmore (Benefits Manager): And in the gap, Tallyhold got us on a call within two days, and their rep did the demo the next morning. So we were already halfway into their onboarding forms by the time you showed up.
Signe Galbraith (Chief People Officer): We are tired. Neither of us wants to run two evaluations. I'm sorry. The demo you gave was good, I could tell it would've worked. It's just the timing.
Rep: Is it final?
Signe Galbraith (Chief People Officer): Pretty much. We signed Monday. If I'd seen it a week earlier, who knows.
Bram Dunmore (Benefits Manager): Yeah. It's a shame.

D251.call_notes:
Rep: Thaddeus, Marisol, hi. Ready for the walkthrough?
Thaddeus Underhill (HR Generalist): Ready. Short on time, so let's go.
Marisol Fairweather (Payroll Manager): Same. I only have until three.
Thaddeus Underhill (HR Generalist): While you're setting up, just so you know where I'm at. We called on Tuesday, and the demo is Thursday. Two days. I was expecting a month. That's what Corvane did, we're still waiting to hear when they can show us anything.
Rep: Happy to be quick.
Marisol Fairweather (Payroll Manager): I'll tell you what I want to see. The off-cycle runs. Bonuses, corrections. Our current setup makes me re-key everything.
Rep: Let me show you that now.
Thaddeus Underhill (HR Generalist): This is what I mean. She asked and you just showed it. No 'I'll follow up'.
Marisol Fairweather (Payroll Manager): Okay. I'm satisfied. How long to get live?
Rep: Five weeks, and I'll assign you an implementation lead today.
Thaddeus Underhill (HR Generalist): That's the clincher for me. A name, a date. We're doing it. Marisol?
Marisol Fairweather (Payroll Manager): Yes. Send the order form.

D252.call_notes:
Rep: Lucian, Fenella, thanks for taking the call. Where do things stand on your end?
Lucian Hollander (Chief People Officer): I'll be direct, and I'll cite the dates, because I think they matter. We had our first conversation on the third of October. You proposed a demo, and the earliest slot was the fourteenth. Eleven days. In that window I had to show my leadership something, so I took the proposal from another vendor and put together a pilot.
Fenella Whitlock (IT Manager): I was the one who set that up. It took me about four days, and it integrates with our existing single sign-on, so it was easy to say yes to.
Lucian Hollander (Chief People Officer): By the time your team showed up on the fourteenth, we'd already migrated roughly 60 of our 142 employees into the other system. I wasn't going to start over, and honestly, nobody had the patience for a second round.
Rep: I understand. Was there anything in the demo itself that fell short?
Lucian Hollander (Chief People Officer): No. It was well done. I told Fenella afterwards that I liked the reporting. But it was a day late. Maybe a week late.
Fenella Whitlock (IT Manager): The wait was the whole thing, really.
Lucian Hollander (Chief People Officer): Yes. Not ideal on either side.
Rep: Thank you for being open about it.
D252.closing_email:
Subject: Following up on our decision

Hi,

Thank you for your time and for the demo on the fourteenth. I wanted to let you know in writing that we have decided to continue with the vendor we began piloting.

To be clear about the reason: eleven days passed between our first call and your demonstration, and in that interval we had already begun a pilot and moved a large share of our employees. Switching at that point was not practical.

I appreciate the professionalism of your team and would welcome the chance to reconnect in future.

Kind regards,
Lucian Hollander

D253.call_notes:
Rep: Marisol, Signe, thanks for taking the call, I wanted to see where you'd got to.
Marisol Cadogan (Director of Operations): Oh, hi. Yes, so, um, I feel a bit awkward, because I think I have to tell you we've moved on. We were talking, what was it, about a week ago? No, longer. Sorry, I'm all over the place today. The first call was a Monday, and the demo wasn't until the Monday after, six days, so we were basically a week out, and in that week things happened.
Signe Jessamy (General Manager): Things happened, yes.
Marisol Cadogan (Director of Operations): Like, Corvane's rep rang me on Wednesday, and I thought, well, I'm waiting on you, but she was keen, and she said she could get us a walkthrough Thursday, and I thought, why not, and then it was, well, it was fine, and then Signe said, let's just do it, because we'd been going back and forth for months and honestly everyone was ready to stop thinking about it.
Signe Jessamy (General Manager): The momentum was gone by the time you came on. I'm sorry. It wasn't your fault. We just wanted it done.
Rep: Did you sign already?
Marisol Cadogan (Director of Operations): We did. Friday. So by the time we had your demo on Monday, we were basically telling you out of politeness. I should have called earlier. Sorry.
Rep: No need. I appreciate the honesty.
Signe Jessamy (General Manager): Thanks for understanding.

D254.call_notes:
Rep: Greta, Signe, thanks for joining.
Greta Santangelo (HR Generalist): Yeah. Let me say this first. We've gone with Corvane.
Rep: Okay. Can you tell me why?
Greta Santangelo (HR Generalist): The wait. Six days. We called you on a Tuesday. You couldn't demo until the following Monday. I know that sounds small.
Signe Underhill (Operations Director): It wasn't small to us. Greta had her whole site team asking every day, when are we switching. She had nothing to tell them.
Greta Santangelo (HR Generalist): Right. I'm in the field half the time. Construction. Five states. I can't sit around.
Rep: And Corvane moved faster?
Greta Santangelo (HR Generalist): They got us in front of someone in a day. We started the trial before you even showed up. Our crews liked it. Done.
Signe Underhill (Operations Director): I wanted to see yours. I really did. But Greta had already told the owners we'd pick one by the end of the week. By Monday it was decided.
Greta Santangelo (HR Generalist): It wasn't the product. I never saw enough of it to judge. That's the shame.
Rep: I appreciate you telling me.
Greta Santangelo (HR Generalist): Sorry. Timing's timing.
Signe Underhill (Operations Director): Yeah. Good luck.

D255.call_notes:
Rep: Idris, Oriel, good afternoon. Thank you for joining.
Idris Ibarra (VP of People): Good afternoon. Thank you. Oriel is our controller, and he has, I believe, a few questions that he would like to put to you directly.
Oriel Ashgrove (Controller): I do. Let me start with the one I care about most. When we run our first payroll on the new system, what is the reconciliation to the general ledger like? Is it manual?
Rep: There is an export, and we map accounts during implementation.
Oriel Ashgrove (Controller): And who does the mapping?
Rep: Your implementation lead sits with you for it.
Oriel Ashgrove (Controller): Good. I wanted a name, not a promise. Second, the contract. What happens if the timeline slips for reasons that are yours?
Rep: The plan has a defined schedule, and we have a remedy clause in the agreement.
Oriel Ashgrove (Controller): Thank you. I find that I have no further objections.
Idris Ibarra (VP of People): Then perhaps I may state my view. The demonstration answered the particular questions I brought, which were about our two shifts and the overtime rules. I was particularly pleased that your support lead replied to me within the hour when I sent a follow-up. And the implementation plan was clear enough that Oriel could review it line by line.
Oriel Ashgrove (Controller): I did. I am supportive.
Idris Ibarra (VP of People): Then we should like to proceed.

D256.call_notes:
Rep: Maren, Ingrid, thanks for hopping on. How's the week?
Maren Thorsen (HR Director): Oh, busy, busy, it's the harvest season for us, well, not literally, we're a brewery, but you know, the fall rush, everybody wants a pumpkin ale. Anyway. So, I wanted to call rather than email, because you've been really good to us.
Ingrid Jessamy (Payroll Manager): They have, they really have.
Maren Thorsen (HR Director): So we're going with Tallyhold. And I want to explain, because I think it'd drive me crazy not to. Our broker, our broker, the one who does our benefits renewals every year, she brought us this bundle. Payroll, benefits, all of it in one package. And she's been with us for, gosh, ten years, and she's never steered us wrong, so when she said look at this one, I looked.
Ingrid Jessamy (Payroll Manager): And honestly, Maren trusts her. I trust Maren. So there we are.
Maren Thorsen (HR Director): It's the bundle she put in front of us, and since she's the one who'll be calling the carriers every year anyway, it just makes sense to have her on our side.
Rep: That makes sense. Was there anything on our side?
Maren Thorsen (HR Director): No, no, nothing like that. You were wonderful. It's about relationships, really.
Ingrid Jessamy (Payroll Manager): Yes. Thank you for everything.

D257.call_notes:
Rep: Mirela, Nadia, thanks for joining. I wanted to find out where the evaluation stands.
Mirela Cadogan (Head of HR): Well, to give you the specifics. We have 106 employees in four states. The demo was supposed to be mid-October. It ended up being the twenty-first of November, sixteen days after our first call, which, I'll say, did not help. But that's a minor point. It's not the reason we're here.
Nadia Brannigan (IT Manager): The reason is that the whole thing is on ice. On the ninth, our parent company announced a restructuring. Every systems project is under review, and there's a hold on anything that touches vendors or contracts until the new structure is clear. That is the direct cause.
Mirela Cadogan (Head of HR): Meanwhile, our sponsor, Dennis, who was the VP who kicked this off, has been moved to a different division. He's still around, but he doesn't own this budget now. I've emailed the new head twice and got nothing back.
Nadia Brannigan (IT Manager): I had finished the security questionnaire, by the way, so that's all ready if it comes back.
Mirela Cadogan (Head of HR): The product wasn't the problem. I want to be clear. Neither was the quote, I checked it against what we pay today and it was a fair comparison. And no, we are not talking to a competitor. We aren't talking to anyone.
Rep: Understood. Is there a rough time to check in?
Mirela Cadogan (Head of HR): I would say the first quarter, maybe February. Nobody knows. I'll tell you when I hear anything.
Nadia Brannigan (IT Manager): Same here.

D258.call_notes:
Rep: Greta, Omar, thanks so much for joining. I hope the week has been manageable.
Greta Galbraith (VP of People): It has, thank you. I will keep this short, since I know you have a full calendar. Omar and I have talked at some length, and we have decided to make a change.
Rep: A change from the current setup?
Greta Galbraith (VP of People): Yes, we are going in a different direction. We wanted to tell you directly, as we have valued the conversations over the last few weeks.
Omar Galbraith (IT Manager): Yes, thank you. Your team has been very helpful with the security questionnaire, and the walk-through was well run.
Rep: That is good to hear. Is there anything you can share about how you reached the decision? It would help us improve.
Greta Galbraith (VP of People): I do not think there is anything specific to say. It has been a considered decision, and we feel good about it. We would simply like to close this out graciously.
Omar Galbraith (IT Manager): Absolutely. No hard feelings at all.
Rep: Of course. I appreciate you telling me personally.
Greta Galbraith (VP of People): Thank you for understanding. Please give our regards to the rest of your team.
Rep: I will. All the best to you both.
Omar Galbraith (IT Manager): And to you. Thank you again.

D259.call_notes:
Rep: Amara, Thaddeus, thank you for jumping on.
Amara Okonkwo (People Operations Lead): Hi. Sorry, I'm running on four hours of sleep, we had a payroll error last week and I'm still cleaning it up. Which is kind of the irony.
Thaddeus Rourke (COO): We're calling because we've decided. We're going with Tallyhold.
Amara Okonkwo (People Operations Lead): And I wanted to tell you why, plainly, because you've been straight with us. Our broker, the one who handles our benefits renewals, sent over their bundle. Payroll, benefits, time tracking, one invoice. She's looked after us for years. I asked her, honestly, which one, and she said this one.
Thaddeus Rourke (COO): It's a lot to take on trust, but we do trust her. She's the one we call at two in the morning when a carrier does something stupid.
Amara Okonkwo (People Operations Lead): It's what she put in front of us. I didn't go shopping for something she hadn't already vetted. I'm too tired to be a hero.
Rep: I understand. Did anything about our product or our quote come into it?
Amara Okonkwo (People Operations Lead): No. The demo was good, you were quick, you answered what I asked. It's not that.
Thaddeus Rourke (COO): It's just that she's the one managing the renewals, and having her in our corner on the software too matters more to me than another feature or two.
Amara Okonkwo (People Operations Lead): Yeah. Sorry to disappoint you.
Rep: No apology necessary.

D260.call_notes:
Rep: Ingrid, Greta, so nice to see you both. I hope the new office is treating you well.
Ingrid Underhill (HR Director): Oh, it's lovely, except the heating, we're all in coats, but anyway. Thanks for hopping on. I wanted to talk through where we are, because I've been going back and forth on it all week, and Greta's been very patient.
Greta Quillfeather (Benefits Manager): Very patient, that's me.
Ingrid Underhill (HR Director): So, the thing is, your yearly figure for our one hundred ninety-six people came to about thirty-nine thousand.
